# What chtypes supports in v2

<!-- Generated by scripts/support-v2/gen.py. Do not edit: regenerate it. -->

Three independent axes, and a combination works only if all three do: the **language** you call from, the **platform** you run on, and the **ClickHouse line** you want answers for. This page states the two the SDK owns and the rule for the third; the lines themselves are on the [per-line support page](https://registry.wavehouse.dev/chtypes/v2/support-matrix.md), published with the builds. Where something is not known it is **support unknown**, which is not the same as unsupported.

## Languages

| Binding    | Package                            | Requires                  | Loads the library with          |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Go         | `github.com/wave-rf/chtypes/go/v2` | Go 1.27+                  | cgo + `dlopen`                  |
| Python     | `chtypes`                          | Python 3.11+              | stdlib `ctypes` (no build step) |
| TypeScript | `@wavehouse/chtypes`               | Node 22.21+, ESM only     | `ffi-rs` (prebuilt)             |
| Rust       | `chtypes`                          | Rust 1.87+ (edition 2024) | `libloading`                    |

All four loaders are `dlopen`, so all four bindings are Unix-only. There is no Windows library and no 32-bit build.

## SDK and ABI

Every v2 SDK speaks ABI generation 2: the `chs_*` function table described under [`spec/abi-v2/`](../spec/abi-v2/). A library is matched to an SDK by the ABI fingerprint its signed statement carries, and the loader refuses a mismatch naming both sides. The fingerprint belongs to a build of the SDK, so this page states none: a copy here could only drift from it.

## Platforms

The library is native code, so a platform works only if the registry serves a build for it. The platforms a fetch recognizes are fixed by [`spec/fetch-v1/constants.json`](../spec/fetch-v1/constants.json):

- `linux-amd64`
- `linux-arm64`
- `darwin-arm64`

A host on any other platform gets `CHTYPES_ARTIFACT_UNPUBLISHED` from a fetch, naming what the registry does offer. On Linux the library needs a glibc at or above the floor its own build records, carried in its signed statement and checked by the loader; a host under it is refused with `CHTYPES_ARTIFACT_INCOMPATIBLE`. musl-based images are in the same position as any platform not listed: support unknown until a build says otherwise.

## ClickHouse lines

One library per ClickHouse line, each carrying that release's own C++. **A line is supported exactly while upstream's [`SECURITY.md`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/SECURITY.md) lists it.** A line upstream no longer lists is retired: its published builds stay served, and they are unsupported. A line the channel's signed per-line document does not name is support unknown.

The artifact producer's publish job renders the full per-line page and serves it with the builds, at <https://registry.wavehouse.dev/chtypes/v2/support-matrix.md>. A 404 there means this channel has not published one yet.

Ask for a line, never a nearest match: a request for a line resolves the newest build of that line and fails if it is absent, rather than quietly handing back a neighbor whose answers differ. List what the registry publishes with the CLI of any binding:

```sh
chtypes list                    # what the registry publishes
chtypes resolve <line>          # each platform's build of the line, verified
```

See [`guides/fetch-v1.md`](guides/fetch-v1.md) for the contract those commands share.
